essence: Make the habit something you look forward to.
modern_lens: Chapter 8 explains that anticipation, not just pleasure, drives behaviour. We repeat the habits we expect to enjoy. Pairing a needed task with something you want, such as a podcast you only hear at the gym or the good coffee you only make during admin time, makes the habit pull you instead of you pushing it.

ideas.name: Exaggerated Rewards Pull Hard
ideas.text: Many modern products amplify what we naturally crave: salt, sugar, novelty, social approval. These exaggerated signals are why junk food and endless feeds are hard to resist. Knowing this lets you choose which rewards your surroundings offer.
ideas.try: Identify one exaggerated reward competing with a good habit and reduce your exposure to it.

ideas.name: Wanting Drives Doing
ideas.text: The brain releases dopamine when it anticipates a reward, not only when it receives one. The craving comes before the action. So the more attractive a habit looks in advance, the more likely you are to start it.
ideas.try: Before a habit you avoid, picture the best part of it for ten seconds.

ideas.name: Temptation Bundling
ideas.text: Link an action you need to do with one you want to do: watch your favourite series only on the exercise bike, or order the nice coffee only while you clear your inbox. The want makes the need more attractive.
ideas.try: Write one bundle: I only [thing I want] while I [thing I need].

ideas.name: Let the Likely Reward the Unlikely
ideas.text: Things you are very likely to do can reinforce things you tend to avoid. If you always check the sports scores, make checking them the step that comes right after the phone call you keep putting off.
ideas.try: Pick a daily pleasure and place it directly after a task you usually postpone.

ideas.name: Stack and Bundle Together
ideas.text: Combine habit stacking with temptation bundling: after my current habit, I do the habit I need; after the habit I need, I do the habit I want. The routine provides the cue and the treat provides the pull.
ideas.try: Write a three-step chain: current habit, needed habit, wanted habit.
